Scenario: Saturday overtime on SMT and PK

Adds 144 open hours over the next two weeks and cuts late orders from 41 to 25 and weighted lateness by 43%. To adopt it, set allow_overtime to Y and list SMT, PK in overtime_work_centers.

Inputs and method

What this schedule was built from, how it was built, and how to refresh it.

Refreshing the schedule

The page is static. New data reaches it when the scheduler runs again and rewrites this file in place.

  1. Drop updated exports into the input folder. Open work orders, material arrivals and shop-floor actuals change most often. Column layouts are listed at the bottom of this page.
  2. Run python schedule.py, or leave python schedule.py --watch running and it reschedules within seconds of any file changing.
  3. Browsers showing this page pick up the new schedule on their next reload, every 5 minutes. No scripts are involved; the page uses an HTML refresh tag.
  4. The schedule it replaces is archived in output/history. Operations inside the frozen window keep the slot the floor was given.
python schedule.py                 # schedule once
python schedule.py --watch         # reschedule when inputs change
python schedule.py --passes 0      # skip the improvement passes
python tools/roll_forward.py --to "2026-06-04 06:00"   # sample data: advance a day

Integrity checks

Every run re-checks the finished schedule against the raw calendars and rules, separately from the engine.

✓
No overlapping operations on any resource
✓
Every operation fits its working time exactly
✓
Changeover time matches the preceding job on every resource
✓
Routing order, move times and transfer batches respected
✓
No order starts before release or before its materials arrive
✓
Nothing is planned in the past
✓
Labor pools never exceed headcount
✓
Every open operation is scheduled or listed as an exception
✓

Built in 24.1 s. 20 of 24 operations in the frozen window held in place.

Sequencing

Orders are ranked by earliest due date, then scheduled one at a time on whichever eligible resource finishes each step first. 30 improvement passes tried moving late orders earlier in the sequence and kept 8 of 54 changes, cutting weighted lateness by 24%.

How the engine works

Time is a grid of 5-minute slots. Each resource gets a working mask from its shift calendar, breaks, plant holidays, optional overtime and planned downtime. An operation uses working slots only, so it pauses overnight and picks up on the next shift.

Run time is quantity times minutes per unit, divided by the resource's stations, efficiency and speed. Changeovers depend on what ran before, from the setup rules and changeover matrix. A job can slot into an earlier gap when it fits and the job after it still has room for its own changeover.

Steps overlap in transfer batches: the next step may start once the first batch is done, but may not finish before the last batch reaches it. Move times, order release and material arrival all hold work back. Shared crews limit how many lines or banks run at once on each shift.

Shop-floor actuals remove finished steps and lock running ones in place. Operations due to start inside the frozen window keep the slot they had in the last published schedule.

For each late order the engine also schedules it alone on an empty plant. If it is still late, the cause is lead time or material; if not, the cause is the queue where it waited longest.

Input layouts

FileColumnsNotes
work_orders.csvwo_id, sku, qty, release, due, priority, customer, tier, order_type, reference, special_requirements, statusOpen orders from ERP. special_requirements such as 10:npi forces a capability on one step. Status Closed drops the order.
actuals.csvwo_id, op_seq, resource_id, status, qty_done, actual_start, actual_endShop-floor feedback. complete removes the step; started locks it on its resource with the quantity left.
materials.csvwo_id, component, supplier, qty_required, eta, statusAnything not On hand holds the first step until its ETA.
routings.csvsku, op_seq, work_center, description, run_min_per_unit, setup_min, required_capability, allow_overlap, move_min_after, order_typesMinutes per unit at one station. order_types limits a step to some order types.

calendars.csvcalendar_id, day, start, end, kind, shift_namekind is shift, break or overtime. An end before the start crosses midnight.
